verses.1: In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah.
verses.2: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi the daughter of Zechariah.
verses.3: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as David his father had done.
verses.4: He removed the high places and broke down the pillars and cut down the sacred pole. He also broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for the Israelites had been burning incense to it up to that time. He called it Nehushtan.
verses.5: He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. No one who was a king in Judah or among those before him was like him.
verses.6: He clung to the LORD and did not turn away from following him. He kept all the commandments that the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.7: The LORD was with him wherever he went, and he defeated the Assyrians and did not serve them.
verses.8: He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from the watchtower of the shepherds to the fortified city.
verses.9: In the fourth year of Hezekiah’s reign, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against Samaria and laid siege to it.
verses.10: After three years of siege, in the sixth year of Hezekiah’s reign, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.
verses.11: The king of Assyria deported the Israelites to Assyria and settled them in Halah, along the Habor River by the city of Gozan and in the cities of the Medes.
verses.12: This happened because the Israelites had not listened to the voice of the LORD their God. They had broken the covenant that the LORD had made with Moses, His servant, and they had not obeyed His commands or done what He had told them.
verses.13: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria marched against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
verses.14: Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the Assyrian king in Lachish, saying, "I have sinned. Please turn back from me. Whatever you place on me, I will bear." The Assyrian king imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
verses.15: Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's palace.
verses.16: At that time, Hezekiah broke off the doors of the temple of the LORD and the doors of the palace and gave them to the Assyrian king.
verses.17: The Assyrian king sent his officials, Tartan, Rab-saris, and Rab-shakeh, with a large army to Jerusalem. They arrived and stood in the upper pool by the road of the fuller's field.
verses.18: They called for the king, and Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to meet them.
verses.19: Rab-shakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah, 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: On what are you relying?'
verses.20: You say, 'Just words and strength for war.' But now, on whom have you relied, since you have rebelled against me?
verses.21: Now you rely on this broken reed, Egypt, on which a man leans, and it pierces him. So it was with Pharaoh king of Egypt for all who relied on him.
verses.22: 'And if you say to me, 'We trust in the LORD our God,' isn't He the one who removed the high places and altars of Hezekiah and said to Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship before this altar in Jerusalem'?
verses.23: 'Now, come to my master, the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you can provide riders for them.
verses.24: 'How could you then repel even a single officer, a minor official of my master? You have placed your trust in Egypt for chariots and for horses!
verses.25: 'Now, have I come up to this place to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD said to me, 'Go up to this land and destroy it.'"
verses.26: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to Rab-shakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in Judean, in the hearing of the people on the wall."
verses.27: Rab-shakeh said to them, "Has my master sent me to speak these words to you and to you alone, and not to the people who are on the wall, who will eat their own excrement and drink their own urine with you?"
verses.28: So Rab-shakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in Judean, "Listen, you who are listening to the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.
verses.29: 'This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot save you from my hand.
verses.30: 'And do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, 'The LORD will surely save us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'"
verses.31: 'Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Each of you may eat from his own vine and fig tree, and each may drink from his own cistern.
verses.32: 'Until I come and take you to a land like your own, a land of grain and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey, and you will live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah, for he deceives you by saying, 'The LORD will save us.'"
verses.33: 'Have any of the gods of the nations saved their lands from my hand? Who among them has been able to deliver his people from me?
verses.34: 'Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they been able to save Samaria from my hand?
verses.35: 'Who among all the gods of the lands has been able to rescue his land from my hand? How then could the LORD rescue Jerusalem from my hand?'"
verses.36: The people were silent and did not answer him, for the king had given orders that they should not answer him.
verses.37: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they told him the words of Rab-shakeh.

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: "Nehushtan" is a transliteration of the Hebrew נְחֻשְׁתָּן, but since the context is clear that it's the name the Israelites gave to the broken bronze serpent, it is retained as is.
- v. 17: "Lachish" is a city, but the Hebrew "מִן־לָכִישׁ" is a prepositional phrase, so the translation is adjusted to maintain clarity.
- v. 26: The term "Aramaic" is used to denote the language of the Assyrian officials, which is appropriate for the context.
- v. 33-35: The rhetorical questions are preserved to reflect the Assyrian taunts and to maintain the tone of the original.
